Answer: D
Reason: The chest X-ray shows complete opacification of the left hemithorax with a significant shift of the trachea and mediastinum to the right (contralateral side). This contralateral deviation indicates a space-occupying lesion, such as a massive pleural effusion, rather than volume loss (atelectasis) which would pull structures toward the opacity. Pneumothorax would appear radiolucent (dark), not opaque.
